text: Components based R6Class. create new component call battery::component function use $extend method existing component. create new R6 class inherit battery::Component directly. connect components normal code, can create one component App added single output using shiny::renderUI rest application can use components. Every component need parent named argument don’t need specify parameters constructor R6Class use initialize function constructor battery use handy constructor function don’t need remember call super$initalize (break components called), use extra parameters need create components. ’re creating child component two options: Second shortcut. need use either proper tree components event propagaion work properly. See example/app.R simple shiny app can run test battery R package.
code: Button <- battery::component(   classname = "Button",   public = list(     count = NULL,     label = NULL,     ## constructor is artifical method so you don't need to call super     ## which you may forget to add     constructor = function(label, canEdit = TRUE) {       self$label <- label       self$connect("click", self$ns("button"))       self$count <- 0       self$on("click", function() {         self$count <- self$count + 1       }, enabled = canEdit)       self$output[[self$ns("buttonOutput")]] <- shiny::renderUI({         self$events$click         tags$div(           tags$span(self$count),           actionButton(self$ns("button"), "click")         )       })     },     render = function() {       tags$div(         class = "button-component",         tags$p(class = "buton-label", self$label),         shiny::uiOutput(self$ns("buttonOutput"))       )     }   ) ) HelloButton <- Button$extend(   classname = "HelloButton",   public = list(     constructor = function() {       super$constructor("hello")     }   ) )  Panel <- battery::Component$extend(   classname = "Panel",   public = list(     title = NULL,     constructor = function(title) {       self$title <- title       Button$new(label = "click Me", component.name = "btn1", parent = self)       HelloButton$new(component.name = "btn2", parent = self)       ## inside each component you have access to output, input and session in self$       ## to make component separated if more then one is used use self$ns to create unique id       self$output[[self$ns("button")]] <- shiny::renderUI({         tags$div(           self$children$btn1$render(),           self$children$btn2$render()         )       })     },     render = function() {       tags$div(         tags$h2(self$title),         tags$div(shiny::uiOutput(self$ns("button")))       )     }   ) )  App <- battery::component(   classname = "App",   public = list(     constructor = function() {       ## for root node you don't need to use ns to create namespace but you can         a <- Panel$new(title = "A", component.name = "panelA", parent = self)         b <- Panel$new(title = "B", component.name = "panelB", parent = self)       self$output[[ self$ns("root") ]] <- shiny::renderUI({         tags$div(           a$render(),           b$render()         )       })     },     render = function() {       tags$div(         titlePanel('Shiny App using Battery R package'),         mainPanel(shiny::uiOutput(self$ns("root")))       )     }   ) ) ## Root component that don't have parent need to be called with shiny session object. server <- function(input, output, session) {   app <- App$new(session = session)   output$root <- renderUI({     app$render()   }) } btn <- Button$new(parent = self) self$appendChild("button", btn) Button$new(parent = self, component.name = "button")

text: Battery provide handling special cases code single place. exceptions created main exported API functions: battery::signal - function can used invoke signal (exception) flow program passed handler used. battery::exceptions - accepts list signal handlers functions two optional arguments. first argument important since contain data exception passed signal. one extra handler error invoked error happen code. battery::withExceptions - function wrap expression special condition may happen, can battery::signal call error code. (note stop() call exactly error code). see example exception mechanism see example/fatalError/app.R Example: adding handle shiny server function. can use battery::signal call handler. Additional error happen, battery component functions, error handler invoked exception. Note error handler place decide happens error. don’t register error handler, battery prints message together origin meta object, errors thrown inside constructors, methods event handlers never lost: important battery catches every error keep rest application running. Without error handler component fails constructor simply stops middle, e.g. renderUI failing line never registered uiOutput stays empty. Also, call battery::signal anywhere components. Example: handler invoked. can use data provide data signal object. can use message just send message. can also use exceptions without using battery components using: default battery::withExceptions used battery give context message error originated. Example error happen constructor meta contain: origin = paste0(self$id, "::constructor") type = "constructor" args = list(...) can give context error singal triggered. important errors want find thrown. Battery wrap methods, handler (using $( method) constructor call battery::withExceptions meta object passed error signals. origin type can check. battery::withExceptions also accepts finally function. invoked exactly , expression done, matter finished normally, raised error signalled exception. Note signal handlers calling handlers, expression resumed signal handled finally invoked point:
code: library(mailR)  battery::exception(list(   error = (cond, meta) {     ## handle error     message("Error ", cond$message, " in ", meta$origin)   },   log = function(cond) {     message(cond$message)   },   sendMail = function(cond) {     send.mail(       from = "noreply@example.com",       to = "admin@example.com",       subject = cond$subject,       body = cond$body     )   } )) thrown in App1::constructor could not find function "undefined.function.call" battery::signal(   'sendMail',   data = list(subject = "This is Email", body = "Lorem Ipsum") ) battery::signal('log', 'This is message') server <- function(input, output, session) {   battery::withExceptions({     battery::signal('log', 'Some message')     # some code     stop() ## this will trigger error handler   },   meta = list(     ## some data for the context   )   session = session) } battery::withExceptions({   battery::signal('log', 'Some message')   ## execution continues here, finally was not called yet }, finally = function() {   ## invoked once, here }, session = session)
